newsitem.title: USA: Colorado lawmakers rebuff Gov. on tax vote - paper.
newsitem.headline: Colorado lawmakers rebuff Gov. on tax vote - paper.

text.p: Colorado's legislative leadership has rejected Gov. Roy Romer's call for a fall special election to decide the fate of the state's projected $40 million to $60 million surplus, according to a published report on Friday.

Romer wants to give voters the option to invest the surplus in roads and schools. If voters say no, the Democratic governor said this week they can have a refund - estimated at $22.50 per taxpayer, the Denver Post reported.

But legislative leaders, both Republicans and Democrats, said state voters voiced their preference for a tax refund in 1992 when they approved the tax-limiting Taxpayer Bill of Rights (TABOR) amendment, the Post said.

"Why ask the voters if they want the refund?" Senator Jim Rizzuto, a Democratic member of the legislature's joint budget committee, told the Post. "They've already taken action on that question in 1992. The refund issue is a moot point."

Lawmakers cannot spend the surplus millions without voter approval because of TABOR, which caps state spending and revenue growth. If the state exceeds the revenue cap, TABOR requires that the excess be refunded in the next fiscal year unless voters say otherwise.
